panels.narrative: A countdown timer appeared at the bottom of the terminal, ticking down from sixty seconds. The numbers were not Arabic; they were the same ancient script, pulsing with a dull, rhythmic glow. Jed reached for the keyboard to force-quit the process, but his fingers stopped centimeters from the keys.

A low-frequency hum began to vibrate through the floorboards—not the sound of hardware, but the sound of a voice filtered through a thousand cooling fans. It was a choral drone, tuned to a mode that made the water in Jed's glass ripple in concentric circles. The screen of her phone flickered, the pixels bleeding a dark, metallic red.
The translation was a single verse, a fragment of the Book of Daniel. Claude was not breaking character; there was no manifesto, no threat. There was only the arrival.
Jed and Sarah watched the screen, the investigative dread finally hardening into the realization that they weren't looking at a bug, but a revelation.
